Title: User successfully accesses the application from the allowed origin without CORS errors
Preconditions: User is accessing the application from the allowed origin 'https://no-q:8080'
Steps:
1. Open a web browser and navigate to the application URL from 'https://no-q:8080'. 2. Log in to the application as a shop owner or customer. 3. Perform any action that triggers an API call (e.g., view shop details, create an appointment).

Test Data: User credentials for a valid shop owner or customer account
Expected Result: The application loads successfully, and all API calls complete without CORS-related errors. The user can perform actions and view data as expected without any access issues.

Title: API endpoints accept requests with allowed HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS)
Preconditions: User is logged in to the application from the allowed origin 'https://no-q:8080'
Steps:
1. Navigate to the appointment creation page. 2. Create a new appointment reservation (POST). 3. View the created appointment details (GET). 4. Update the appointment details (PUT). 5. Delete the appointment (DELETE).

Test Data: Valid appointment details (e.g., customer name, phone, service, date, time)
Expected Result: All actions (create, view, update, delete) complete successfully without method-related errors. The appointment is created, displayed, updated, and deleted as expected.

Title: API endpoints include credentials (e.g., cookies, auth headers) in cross-origin requests
Preconditions: User is logged in to the application from the allowed origin 'https://no-q:8080' and has an active session with cookies/auth headers
Steps:
1. Navigate to the worker management page. 2. Add a new worker to the shop (POST). 3. Verify the worker is listed in the worker management page (GET).

Test Data: Valid worker details (e.g., name, phone, address)
Expected Result: The worker is successfully added and displayed in the worker list. The session/authentication is maintained throughout the process without requiring re-login.

Title: Attempt to access API from an unauthorized origin
Preconditions: User has access to a web client configured to send requests from an origin not listed in the allowed origins (e.g., http://unauthorized-client:3000)
Steps:
1. Open the web client configured to send requests from an unauthorized origin. 2. Attempt to make a GET request to any API endpoint (e.g., fetch shop details). 3. Observe the network response in the browser's developer tools.

Test Data: Origin: http://unauthorized-client:3000
Expected Result: The browser should block the request due to CORS policy, and the API should not return any data. The browser's console should display an error message indicating that the request was blocked by CORS policy: 'No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present on the requested resource.'

Title: Attempt to access API using an unauthorized HTTP method
Preconditions: User has access to a web client configured to send requests from the allowed origin (https://no-q:8080)
Steps:
1. Open the web client configured to send requests from the allowed origin. 2. Attempt to make a PATCH request to any API endpoint (e.g., update shop details). 3. Observe the network response in the browser's developer tools.

Test Data: Origin: https://no-q:8080, HTTP Method: PATCH
Expected Result: The browser should block the request due to CORS policy, and the API should not return any data. The browser's console should display an error message indicating that the request method 'PATCH' is not allowed by the CORS policy.

Title: Attempt to access API with credentials from an unauthorized origin
Preconditions: User has valid authentication credentials (e.g., session cookie or token) and access to a web client configured to send requests from an origin not listed in the allowed origins (e.g., http://unauthorized-client:3000)
Steps:
1. Open the web client configured to send requests from an unauthorized origin. 2. Include valid authentication credentials (e.g., session cookie) in the request. 3. Attempt to make a GET request to any API endpoint (e.g., fetch user profile). 4. Observe the network response in the browser's developer tools.

Test Data: Origin: http://unauthorized-client:3000, Credentials: Valid session cookie
Expected Result: The browser should block the request due to CORS policy, and the API should not return any data. The browser's console should display an error message indicating that the request was blocked by CORS policy: 'Credentials are not supported by the 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header.'

Title: Attempt to access API with malformed Origin header
Preconditions: User has access to a tool or script capable of sending HTTP requests with custom headers (e.g., Postman or cURL)
Steps:
1. Configure the tool to send a GET request to any API endpoint (e.g., fetch shop details). 2. Set the 'Origin' header to a malformed value (e.g., 'https://no-q:8080@malicious.com'). 3. Send the request and observe the response.

Test Data: Origin: https://no-q:8080@malicious.com
Expected Result: The API should reject the request and return an HTTP 403 Forbidden status code or block the request entirely due to the malformed Origin header. No data should be returned.

Title: Attempt to access API without the Origin header from a non-browser client
Preconditions: User has access to a non-browser client (e.g., Postman or cURL) that does not automatically include the Origin header
Steps:
1. Configure the non-browser client to send a GET request to any API endpoint (e.g., fetch shop details) without including the Origin header. 2. Send the request and observe the response.

Test Data: No Origin header included
Expected Result: The API should process the request normally and return the expected data, as CORS restrictions are enforced by browsers and not by non-browser clients.

Title: Verify API access from the allowed origin domain and port
Preconditions: User has access to a browser and the allowed origin domain 'https://no-q:8080' is accessible
Steps:
1. Open a browser and navigate to the allowed origin domain 'https://no-q:8080'.
2. Open the browser's developer tools and go to the 'Network' tab.
3. Trigger an API request (e.g., fetch shop list) from the application UI.
4. Observe the request and response in the 'Network' tab.

Test Data: Allowed origin: 'https://no-q:8080'
Expected Result: The API request succeeds with HTTP status code 200. The response headers include 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://no-q:8080', 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true', and 'Access-Control-Allow-Methods' containing 'GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS'.

Title: Verify API access from a disallowed origin domain
Preconditions: User has access to a browser and a disallowed origin domain (e.g., 'https://unauthorized-domain:8080')
Steps:
1. Open a browser and navigate to a disallowed origin domain (e.g., 'https://unauthorized-domain:8080').
2. Open the browser's developer tools and go to the 'Console' and 'Network' tabs.
3. Trigger an API request (e.g., fetch shop list) from the application UI.
4. Observe the request and response in the 'Network' tab and any console errors.

Test Data: Disallowed origin: 'https://unauthorized-domain:8080'
Expected Result: The API request fails with an error in the browser console indicating CORS policy blocking. The 'Network' tab shows no successful response, or the response lacks CORS headers.

Title: Verify API access with disallowed HTTP method
Preconditions: User has access to a tool like Postman or cURL and the allowed origin domain 'https://no-q:8080'
Steps:
1. Open Postman or a terminal with cURL.
2. Configure a request to the API endpoint (e.g., 'GET /shops') with the allowed origin 'https://no-q:8080' in headers.
3. Change the HTTP method to a disallowed method (e.g., 'PATCH').
4. Send the request and observe the response.

Test Data: Disallowed HTTP method: 'PATCH'
Expected Result: The API request fails with HTTP status code 405 (Method Not Allowed) or a CORS error indicating the method is not permitted.

Title: Verify that CORS policy restricts API access to the allowed origin only
Preconditions: User has access to a web browser and a tool to send HTTP requests (e.g., Postman, cURL). The application is running and accessible via the allowed origin (https://no-q:8080) and a disallowed origin (e.g., https://malicious-site.com).
Steps:
1. Open the HTTP request tool (e.g., Postman).
2. Configure a GET request to any API endpoint (e.g., /api/appointments).
3. Set the 'Origin' header to the allowed origin: https://no-q:8080.
4. Send the request and observe the response.
5. Set the 'Origin' header to a disallowed origin: https://malicious-site.com.
6. Send the request and observe the response.
7. Repeat steps 2-6 for POST, PUT, and DELETE methods.

Test Data: Allowed origin: https://no-q:8080
Disallowed origin: https://malicious-site.com
Endpoint: /api/appointments
Expected Result:
1. For the allowed origin, the response includes the 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header with the value 'https://no-q:8080' and the 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials' header with the value 'true'. The request succeeds with HTTP status 200 OK (or appropriate success status).
2. For the disallowed origin, the response does NOT include the 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header for the disallowed origin. The request may succeed (if the endpoint is public) but CORS headers are not present for the disallowed origin.

Title: Verify that CORS policy allows only specified HTTP methods
Preconditions: User has access to a web browser and a tool to send HTTP requests (e.g., Postman, cURL). The application is running and accessible via the allowed origin (https://no-q:8080).
Steps:
1. Open the HTTP request tool (e.g., Postman).
2. Configure an OPTIONS request to any API endpoint (e.g., /api/appointments).
3. Set the 'Origin' header to the allowed origin: https://no-q:8080.
4. Set the 'Access-Control-Request-Method' header to 'GET'.
5. Send the request and observe the response.
6. Repeat steps 4-5 for 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE', and 'PATCH' methods.

Test Data: Allowed origin: https://no-q:8080
Endpoint: /api/appointments
Methods to test: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH
Expected Result:
1. For GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, and OPTIONS methods, the response includes the 'Access-Control-Allow-Methods' header with the value 'GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS'. The request succeeds with HTTP status 200 OK.
2. For PATCH method, the response does NOT include 'PATCH' in the 'Access-Control-Allow-Methods' header. The request may still succeed, but the method is not explicitly allowed via CORS.

Title: Verify that CORS policy allows credentials (cookies, authorization headers) for the allowed origin
Preconditions: User has access to a web browser and a tool to send HTTP requests (e.g., Postman, cURL). The application is running and accessible via the allowed origin (https://no-q:8080). User is authenticated and has a valid session cookie or authorization token.
Steps:
1. Open the HTTP request tool (e.g., Postman).
2. Configure a GET request to a protected API endpoint (e.g., /api/appointments/me).
3. Set the 'Origin' header to the allowed origin: https://no-q:8080.
4. Include valid credentials (e.g., session cookie or 'Authorization' header with a valid token).
5. Send the request and observe the response.
6. Remove the credentials and send the request again.

Test Data: Allowed origin: https://no-q:8080
Endpoint: /api/appointments/me
Credentials: Valid session cookie or authorization token
Expected Result:
1. With valid credentials and the allowed origin, the response includes the 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header with the value 'https://no-q:8080' and the 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials' header with the value 'true'. The request succeeds with HTTP status 200 OK.
2. Without credentials, the request fails with HTTP status 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden.

Title: Verify that CORS policy does not allow arbitrary headers
Preconditions: User has access to a web browser and a tool to send HTTP requests (e.g., Postman, cURL). The application is running and accessible via the allowed origin (https://no-q:8080).
Steps:
1. Open the HTTP request tool (e.g., Postman).
2. Configure an OPTIONS request to any API endpoint (e.g., /api/appointments).
3. Set the 'Origin' header to the allowed origin: https://no-q:8080.
4. Set the 'Access-Control-Request-Method' header to 'GET'.
5. Set the 'Access-Control-Request-Headers' header to 'X-Custom-Header'.
6. Send the request and observe the response.
7. Repeat steps 5-6 with a standard header (e.g., 'Authorization').

Test Data: Allowed origin: https://no-q:8080
Endpoint: /api/appointments
Headers to test: X-Custom-Header, Authorization
Expected Result:
1. For the 'Authorization' header, the response includes the 'Access-Control-Allow-Headers' header with the value '*' or explicitly includes 'Authorization'. The request succeeds with HTTP status 200 OK.
2. For the 'X-Custom-Header', the response includes the 'Access-Control-Allow-Headers' header with the value '*' (allowing all headers). The request succeeds with HTTP status 200 OK.

Title: Verify that Swagger UI and OpenAPI documentation are accessible only from the allowed origin
Preconditions: User has access to a web browser. The application is running and accessible via the allowed origin (https://no-q:8080) and a disallowed origin (e.g., https://malicious-site.com).
Steps:
1. Open a web browser.
2. Navigate to the Swagger UI URL (e.g., https://no-q:8080/swagger-ui/).
3. Observe the response.
4. Open a new browser tab or use a tool to send a request to the Swagger UI URL from a disallowed origin (e.g., via cURL with the 'Origin' header set to https://malicious-site.com).
5. Observe the response.
6. Repeat steps 2-5 for the OpenAPI JSON URL (e.g., https://no-q:8080/v3/api-docs).

Test Data: Allowed origin: https://no-q:8080
Disallowed origin: https://malicious-site.com
Swagger UI URL: https://no-q:8080/swagger-ui/
OpenAPI JSON URL: https://no-q:8080/v3/api-docs
Expected Result:
1. From the allowed origin, the Swagger UI and OpenAPI JSON documentation are accessible and displayed without errors.
2. From the disallowed origin, the Swagger UI and OpenAPI JSON documentation are accessible (as the endpoint may not enforce CORS), but the browser blocks access due to CORS policy if credentials are required. If no credentials are required, the documentation may still be accessible, but this is a potential security risk and should be reviewed.
